<!-- ====================================================================== -->

---
title: Integrations
description: Wire Sponsio into your agent framework.
---

# Integrations

Sponsio works with any agent framework in Python and TypeScript. Each integration intercepts tool calls at the framework's native hook point. All integrations share the same LTL engine and produce identical block / allow decisions. See `tests/cross_language/` for cross-language validation.

## At a glance

### Python

| Framework | Factory | Tool wrapping | Lines to add |
|---|---|---|---|
| LangGraph | `from sponsio.langgraph import Sponsio` | `guard.wrap(tools)` | 3 |
| Claude Agent SDK | `from sponsio.claude_agent import Sponsio` | `guard.hooks()` (zero wrapping) | 2 |
| OpenAI SDK | `from sponsio.openai import Sponsio` (or `patch_openai`) | automatic response checks | 2 |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | `from sponsio.agents import Sponsio` | `guard.wrap(tools)` | 3 |
| Vercel AI SDK | `from sponsio.vercel_ai import Sponsio` | `guard.wrap()` (middleware) | 2 |
| CrewAI | `from sponsio.crewai import Sponsio` | `guard.wrap(tools)` | 3 |
| Google ADK | `from sponsio.google_adk import Sponsio` | `guard.wrap(tools)` | 3 |
| MCP | `from sponsio.mcp import MCPContractProxy` | `proxy.call_tool()` | 3 |
| No framework | `sponsio.Sponsio(contracts=[...])` | `guard.guard_before()` / `guard_after()` | 3 |

### TypeScript (native, same engine, no server)

| Framework | Import | Integration |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Agent SDK | `@sponsio/sdk/claude-agent` | `sponsioHooks(guard)` |
| Vercel AI SDK | `@sponsio/sdk/vercel-ai` | `sponsioMiddleware(guard)` |
| OpenAI SDK | `@sponsio/sdk/openai` | `wrapOpenAI(client, guard)` |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | `@sponsio/sdk/openai-agents` | `wrapAgentsTools(tools, guard)` |
| LangChain.js | `@sponsio/sdk/langchain` | `wrapTools(tools, guard)` |
| Google ADK | `@sponsio/sdk/google-adk` | `wrapGoogleAdkTools(tools, guard)` |

## Python example: LangGraph

```python
from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
from sponsio import contract
from sponsio.langgraph import Sponsio

guard = Sponsio(
    agent_id="my_bot",
    contracts=[
        contract("policy gate before refund")
            .assume("called `issue_refund`")
            .guarantees("must call `check_policy` before `issue_refund`"),
    ],
)

agent = create_react_agent(model, guard.wrap(tools))
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [("user", "process refund")]})
guard.print_summary()
```

For existing graphs, use `wrap_graph()`:

```python
guard = Sponsio(config="sponsio.yaml", agent_id="bot")
graph = build_my_graph()
graph = guard.wrap_graph(graph)
```

`wrap_graph()` checks every node against the contracts before the node body runs. In enforce mode a stopping verdict raises `ToolCallBlocked` out of `invoke()` / `stream()` (and their async and batch forms) and the node never executes. The contracts see node names as actions; tool calls made inside a node are gated individually only when that node's tools come from `guard.wrap(tools)`.

The pattern is the same for CrewAI, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, and Vercel AI SDK. Swap the import for the matching `sponsio.<framework>` namespace and call `guard.wrap(tools)`.

## TypeScript example: Claude Agent SDK

```typescript
import { ClaudeAgent } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk";
import { Sponsio } from "@sponsio/sdk";
import { sponsioHooks } from "@sponsio/sdk/claude-agent";

const guard = new Sponsio({
  agentId: "my_bot",
  contracts: ["must call `check_policy` before `issue_refund`"],
});

const agent = new ClaudeAgent({
  hooks: sponsioHooks(guard),
});
```

## Custom loop (no framework)

```python
import sponsio
from sponsio import contract

guard = sponsio.Sponsio(
    agent_id="my_agent",
    contracts=[
        contract("identity check before transfer")
            .assume("called `transfer_funds`")
            .guarantees("must call `verify_identity` before `transfer_funds`"),
    ],
)

while not done:
    tool_name, args = llm_decide_next_action()
    result = guard.guard_before(tool_name, args)
    if result.stop_original:      # not result.blocked: see note below
        llm_messages.append(f"Action blocked: {result.det_violations[0].message}")
        continue
    output = execute_tool(tool_name, args)
    guard.guard_after(tool_name, output)
```

**Gate on `result.stop_original`, not `result.blocked`.** A `redirect_to_safe`
violation leaves `blocked` False and `allowed` True, because the agent flow can
continue down the safe path. A loop that gates on `blocked` falls through and
runs the exact call the contract forbade. `stop_original` folds hard blocks and
redirects together, so it fails closed. If you want the substitution itself, see
[Redirect to safe](#redirect-to-safe-v02).

## Tool policy: default-deny + proactive filtering (v0.2)

Sponsio's `tool_policy` section lets you declare an allow-list once and have it surface either reactively (the AI tries a denied tool, gets blocked at call time) or proactively (the denied tool never reaches the AI's tool menu).

```yaml
tool_policy:
  default: deny             # allow (default) | deny
  approved: [search, read_file, list_dir]
  enforcement: reactive     # reactive (default) | proactive
```

Or inline:

```python
guard = sponsio.Sponsio(
    contracts=[...],
    tool_policy={"default": "deny", "approved": ["search"], "enforcement": "proactive"},
)
```

### What `proactive` does per adapter

Under `enforcement: proactive`, `guard.wrap(tools)` drops tools outside `approved` once, at wrap time. Where the framework lets Sponsio change the tool list before each model call, the adapter also offers only the tools the session's state allows on that turn (`guard.tools_for_turn`), so `must_precede(A, B)` puts B on the menu only after A has run, and `no_reversal(A, B)` takes it off again. Observe mode filters nothing. Every call is still decided by `guard_before`.

| Adapter | Per-turn tool list |
|---|---|
| OpenAI SDK (chat, responses) | `guard.wrap(client)` narrows `tools=` on every `create` / `parse`. |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | Each tool from `guard.wrap(tools)` gets an `is_enabled` check, which the SDK runs every turn. |
| LangGraph | `create_react_agent(guard.dynamic_model(model, tools), guard.wrap(tools))` binds the allowed tools on every model call. |
| Google ADK | `Agent(before_model_callback=guard.before_model_callback, tools=guard.wrap(tools))` removes the others from each model request. |
| Claude Agent SDK | The SDK fixes tools for a whole query. Build each query's options with `guard.query_options(names)`; the hooks decide every call inside it. |
| CrewAI | Tools are fixed for a task. Pass `guard.tools_for_turn(...)` when building each task; calls are still checked. |
| Vercel AI SDK | Filter `tools` before each request with `guard.tools_for_turn(...)`. |
| Custom loop (no framework) | `guard.tools_for_turn(...)` (or `guard.filter_tools(...)`) before each turn (see below). |
| MCP | The [MCP gateway](../reference/daemon.md#mcp-gateway) lists per session state and refuses unlisted tools. |

### Custom loop with per-turn proactive filtering

`guard.filter_tools(candidates)` returns the subset of candidate tool names whose call would not be blocked right now. The call is pure (no events, logs, callbacks, or perf samples) and evaluates *all* contracts including temporal ones. Call it before each LLM turn:

```python
import sponsio

guard = sponsio.Sponsio(
    agent_id="my_agent",
    contracts=["must call `verify_identity` before `transfer_funds`"],
    tool_policy={"default": "deny", "approved": ["verify_identity", "transfer_funds"]},
)

ALL_TOOLS = [verify_identity_tool, transfer_funds_tool, debug_tool, ...]
ALL_NAMES = [t.name for t in ALL_TOOLS]

while not done:
    # Per-turn refresh: returns only tools legal under the current trace.
    legal_names = set(guard.filter_tools(ALL_NAMES))
    legal_tools = [t for t in ALL_TOOLS if t.name in legal_names]
    tool_name, args = llm_decide_next_action(messages, tools=legal_tools)
    result = guard.guard_before(tool_name, args)
    if result.stop_original:      # not result.blocked: see note below
        messages.append(f"Action blocked: {result.det_violations[0].message}")
        continue
    output = execute_tool(tool_name, args)
    guard.guard_after(tool_name, output)
```

The difference from `wrap()`-time filtering: `filter_tools` is called each turn and consults the live trace, so `must_precede(A, B)` opens B in the menu only *after* A fires. This is the most thorough proactive option Sponsio offers; it requires you to own the agent loop.

## Rules in the daemon (`backend="daemon"`)

By default the guard decides in your process, from contracts your process holds. With `backend="daemon"`, the Sponsio daemon decides: the rules are its library named after `agent_id` (`<plugin-root>/<agent_id>/sponsio.yaml`), the session's history is kept in the daemon, and the mode is the daemon's (`hosts: {sdk: {mode: observe}}` in [`daemon.yaml`](../reference/daemon.md#daemonyaml)). Code running in the agent's process can send events, but cannot change the rules, the mode or the history.

```python
from sponsio.langgraph import Sponsio

guard = Sponsio(agent_id="support-bot", backend="daemon")
agent = create_react_agent(guard.dynamic_model(model, tools), guard.wrap(tools))
```

- No contracts, config or `tool_policy` are passed; the library is the daemon's.
- Per-turn tool lists (above) are on, whatever `tool_policy` says.
- A call the daemon does not answer is blocked, and `tools_for_turn` offers nothing. The SDK does not start a daemon; run `sponsio daemon run --detach` as part of the service.
- `rotate_session()` starts a new, empty history in the daemon.

## Redirect to safe (v0.2)

`redirect_to_safe(unsafe, safe)` substitutes a forbidden tool call with a pre-approved one instead of blocking the agent outright. The model can continue, just not down the unsafe path.

```python
from sponsio import contract
from sponsio.patterns import redirect_to_safe

guard = sponsio.Sponsio(
    contracts=[
        contract("trash instead of rm")
            .guarantees(redirect_to_safe("rm_rf", "trash")),

        # Conditional redirect: only large refunds get rerouted.
        contract("large refunds go to review")
            .assume("called `issue_refund`")
            .guarantees(redirect_to_safe("issue_refund", "log_refund_request")),
    ],
)
```

When the agent calls `rm_rf`, Sponsio:

1. Rolls back the `rm_rf` event from the trace so downstream counters (`rate_limit`, `count_at_most`) don't tick on the attempted call.
2. Surfaces `result.redirected=True` + `result.redirected_to="trash"` from `guard_before`.
3. The adapter invokes `trash` with the model's original arguments. The trace records the `trash` call (via the normal `guard_before(safe, args)` path), so the audit log reflects what actually executed.

The model sees the safe tool's result, not an error. Substitution is transparent unless the safe tool returns something the model cannot interpret (schema mismatch).

### Constraints

- Both `unsafe` and `safe` must be registered with your framework. Sponsio does NOT synthesize tools.
- The safe tool should accept the same arguments as the unsafe one. If schemas diverge, the adapter passes args verbatim; the user is responsible for compatibility.
- A `redirect → blocked` chain (safe tool also violates a different contract) raises a hard block. Sponsio does not chain redirects to avoid loops.
- Self-redirect (`unsafe == safe`) is rejected loudly via `ToolCallBlocked`. The pattern factory already rejects `redirect_to_safe("X", "X")` at construction; this guard catches the case where a user wired `RedirectToSafe(safe="X")` directly via `policy={}` and bound it to a contract that triggers on tool `X`.
- A `redirect → redirect` chain (`safe` tool itself has a `redirect_to_safe` contract pointing elsewhere) is also rejected. Resolve the chain by pointing the original `unsafe` directly at the final safe tool.

### Interaction with other contracts on the same tool

If a tool has both a `redirect_to_safe` contract AND another contract (e.g. `must_precede`, `count_at_most`) that fires on the same call, the LangGraph adapter takes the **redirect path first** before checking for a block. The model never sees the block message because the call gets substituted; the substitute call is then checked against everything else.

This means a `must_precede(check_policy, issue_refund)` contract paired with `redirect_to_safe("issue_refund", "log_refund_request")` will effectively skip the ordering check for `issue_refund` (the call gets redirected to `log_refund_request` immediately, and `must_precede` only applies to `issue_refund`'s actual execution which never happens). This is by design: redirecting and refusing are conflicting outcomes, and the redirect was your explicit intent for that tool.

If you want both behaviors, write the `must_precede` against the safe tool (`must_precede(check_policy, log_refund_request)`), or use the framework-agnostic `guard.guard_before(unsafe_tool, args)` inspection in a custom loop where you can branch on `check.blocked` before `check.redirected`.

### What `redirect_to_safe` does per adapter

| Adapter | Redirect behavior |
|---|---|
| LangGraph | Built in. `wrap()` indexes tools by name; on redirect the wrapped `ToolNode` invokes the safe tool's `func` / `coroutine` with the model's original kwargs. Unknown safe tool name raises `ToolCallBlocked`. |
| CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, Vercel AI, Claude Agent SDK | Surface only: `result.redirected_to` is set on the `CheckResult`. Adapter-side dispatch lands in a follow-up release. For now, custom loops can read `result.redirected_to` and call the substitute tool themselves. |
| Custom loop (no framework) | Read `check.redirected_to`, look up the safe tool in your registry, call it with the same args. See snippet below. |

```python
# Custom loop pattern that honors redirect_to_safe outcomes
check = guard.guard_before(tool_name, args)
if check.redirected and check.redirected_to:
    actual = check.redirected_to
    check2 = guard.guard_before(actual, args)
    if check2.allowed:
        output = registry[actual](**args)
        guard.guard_after(actual, output)
elif check.blocked:
    messages.append(f"blocked: {check.det_violations[0].message}")
elif check.allowed:
    output = registry[tool_name](**args)
    guard.guard_after(tool_name, output)
```

## Framework-specific notes

### Claude Agent SDK

`guard.hooks()` plugs into `ClaudeAgentOptions(hooks=...)` directly. No tool wrapping needed.

### OpenAI SDK

`patch_openai()` returns a guard whose every `client.chat.completions.create(...)` / `parse(...)` and `client.responses.create(...)` / `parse(...)` is checked automatically; `guard.wrap(client)` does the same for one client instance. `stream=True` raises on every guarded method, because tool calls in a stream can only be checked after the caller's loop has assembled and run them. The `with_raw_response` / `with_streaming_response` forms are checked too; if a call must stop, the guard raises `ToolCallBlocked`, since the raw body cannot be rewritten.

**Not covered:** the Assistants API (`client.beta.threads` runs), the Realtime API (`client.realtime`) and Batches (`client.batches`). Tool calls through those surfaces are not checked. Call `guard.guard_before(name, args)` in your own executor before running them. Set `SPONSIO_OPENAI_STRICT_TOOL_ARGS=1` to fail closed when the model returns malformed JSON in `tool_call.function.arguments`. Default warns and degrades.

### Google ADK

`functools.wraps` preserves the original signatures, so ADK's introspection still works. Both sync and `async` tools are supported. Blocked calls return `{"status": "error", "error_message": "BLOCKED..."}` instead of executing the wrapped function, so the model sees a normal tool result and can self-correct.

### MCP

MCP is a tool transport, not an agent framework. Use `guard_before()` / `guard_after()` directly, or wrap an MCP client transparently:

```python
from sponsio.mcp import MCPContractProxy

proxy = MCPContractProxy(mcp_client=client, system=system)
result = await proxy.call_tool("send_email", {"to": "user@example.com"})
```

## Config-driven (every framework)

All integrations support loading contracts from a YAML file:

```python
from sponsio.langgraph import Sponsio

guard = Sponsio(config="sponsio.yaml", agent_id="my_bot")
```

See [Config yaml reference](../reference/config-yaml.md) for the YAML specification.

## Long-running agents

The trace is append-only during a session. For 24/7 services, call `guard.rotate_session()` periodically to cap memory and keep the verifier's atom caches fresh.

```python
for turn_idx, user_msg in enumerate(conversation):
    response = agent_step(user_msg)
    if turn_idx > 0 and turn_idx % 1000 == 0:
        guard.rotate_session()
```

Rotation preserves the contract set, perf tracker aggregates, callbacks, and dashboard or OTEL wiring. It clears `trace.events`, atom caches, violations, and pending liveness obligations. Whole-trace formulas like `F(response)` cannot survive rotation. `rotate_session()` flushes pending liveness as violations before wiping. Pass `require_finish_session=True` to fail loudly when finalisation is skipped.

Pick a cadence: turn-based (every N turns), wall-clock (every T minutes), or semantic (at the natural end of a conversation). Aim for `N × avg_tool_calls ≈ 10000` events per window.

## OTEL export

```python
from sponsio.integrations.otel import OTelExporter
from sponsio.langgraph import Sponsio

exporter = OTelExporter(endpoint="https://your-otel-backend/v1/traces")
guard = Sponsio(contracts=[...], otel_exporter=exporter)
```

Schema and dashboard wiring: [reference/observability.md](../reference/observability.md).


<!-- ====================================================================== -->
<!-- FILE: docs/reference/cli.md  -->
<!-- ====================================================================== -->

---
title: CLI reference
description: Sponsio's CLI commands, arguments, and options.
---

# CLI reference

Every `sponsio` command exits 0 on success and 1 on failure (parse error, violation, missing input). For LLM-backed commands, install the LLM extra: `pip install --pre "sponsio[llm]"`. API keys come from environment variables only.

## sponsio scan

Scan source code or policy documents to discover contracts.

```bash
sponsio scan PATHS... [--llm] [--policy DOC] [-o sponsio.yaml]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--agent`, `-a` | Agent ID (default: `agent`) |
| `--llm` | Enable LLM inference. Auto-detects provider from env. |
| `--model`, `-m` | LLM model name (default: provider default) |
| `--provider` | `openai`, `anthropic`, or `gemini` |
| `--base-url` | OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint (Ollama, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Together, Groq, vLLM, Azure) |
| `--out`, `-o` | Output file (default: `./sponsio.yaml`; `-o -` for stdout) |
| `--append` | Append to existing file instead of overwriting |
| `--policy`, `-p` | Policy document(s), repeatable |

### Provider matrix

| Provider | Env var | Default model | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemini | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` | `gemini-2.0-flash` | 1500 requests/day free tier |
| Anthropic | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022` | `pip install anthropic` |
| OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `gpt-4o-mini` | |
| Ollama (local) | none | (set `--model`) | `--base-url http://localhost:11434/v1` |
| OpenRouter / DeepSeek / Together / Groq / Cerebras / Fireworks / vLLM / Azure | provider's key | (set `--model`) | `--base-url https://...` against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint |

Auto-detection precedence (when `--provider` is unset): explicit `--base-url` resolves to `openai`; else `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` resolves to `anthropic`; else `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` resolves to `gemini`; else `OPENAI_API_KEY` resolves to `openai`.

```bash
# Rule-based scan, no LLM
sponsio scan src/agents/

# With LLM and policy
sponsio scan src/agents/ --policy security.md --llm -o sponsio.yaml

# Local model via Ollama
sponsio scan src/ --llm --base-url http://localhost:11434/v1 --model llama3.1
```

### TypeScript scanner

The Python AST scanner only parses Python. For Node.js agents, use `@sponsio/sdk`:

```bash
npx @sponsio/sdk ./src --out tools.json
sponsio scan tools.json --out sponsio.yaml
```

The TS scanner statically understands Vercel's `tool({...})`, LangChain's `DynamicStructuredTool`, LangGraph.js's `tool(fn, cfg)`, and common Zod patterns. See [`ts/packages/sdk/README.md`](https://github.com/sponsio-labs/sponsio/tree/main/ts/packages/sdk) for the full matrix.

## sponsio init

Interactive 4-axis project setup wizard. Walks through framework / hosts / skills / mode, writes `sponsio.yaml` in the chosen mode, runs `sponsio doctor`, and prints the agent-entry patch.

```bash
sponsio init [PATH]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `PATH` | Target directory (default: current). Writes `sponsio.yaml` if not present. |
| `--plan PICKS` | Print the would-run commands for these picks. Used by IDE-agent wizards for dry-run previews. |
| `--apply PICKS` | Run non-interactively. Picks format: `framework=<name>;ides=<ide>:<level>,<ide>:<level>;mode=observe\|enforce` where `<level>` is `none`, `skill`, or `full`. Legacy form with separate `hosts=<a>,<b>;skills=<a>,<b>` lists is still accepted (`hosts=` ↔ level `full`, `skills=` ↔ level `skill`). |
| `--no-demo` | Skip the post-install demo offer. |

```bash
sponsio init .                                                              # interactive
sponsio init . --apply "framework=langgraph;mode=observe"                   # non-interactive, no IDE wiring
sponsio init . --apply "framework=langgraph;ides=claude-code:full;mode=observe"   # + Claude Code plugin (full)
sponsio init . --plan "framework=crewai;ides=cursor:skill"                  # dry-run preview
```

See [getting-started/first-contract.md](../getting-started/first-contract.md) for the typical interactive flow.

## sponsio onboard

One-shot project wire-up: composes `init` + `scan` + `doctor` into a single command so first-time users don't have to learn three subcommands. Detects the framework, picks the best available LLM provider (env → `OPENAI_BASE_URL` → local Ollama → none), writes `sponsio.yaml` in observe mode with an inferred contract set, then prints the framework-specific agent-entry patch.

```bash
sponsio onboard [TARGET] [--agent NAME] [--mode observe|enforce] [--force]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `TARGET` | File or directory to scan (default: current). |
| `--mode` | Runtime mode written into `sponsio.yaml`. Omit to be prompted; `observe` is the safe default. |
| `--force` | Overwrite an existing `sponsio.yaml` without prompting. |
| `--no-probe-ollama` | Skip the `localhost:11434` liveness probe. |
| `--no-doctor` | Skip the post-onboard `sponsio doctor` run. |
| `--emit-context` | Skip the LLM step; emit the structured inputs as JSON for the `sponsio` skill. Pair with `sponsio prompt onboard`. |
| `--json` | Emit the structured `OnboardReport` as JSON. |

```bash
sponsio onboard
sponsio onboard src/ --agent customer_bot
sponsio onboard --force --no-probe-ollama
```

## sponsio validate

Parse-check contract strings. CI-friendly.

```bash
sponsio validate [CONTRACTS...] [--config sponsio.yaml] [--agent NAME] [--json]
```

```bash
sponsio validate "tool \`check_policy\` must precede \`issue_refund\`"
sponsio validate --config sponsio.yaml --json
```

## sponsio check

Run contracts against a saved trace file.

```bash
sponsio check --trace FILE [CONTRACTS...] [--config sponsio.yaml] [--agent NAME] [--json]
```

## sponsio patterns

List the deterministic pattern catalog.

```bash
sponsio patterns [--search KEYWORD] [--json]
```

## sponsio demo

Replay a packaged unsafe-trajectory scenario.

```bash
sponsio demo [--scenario NAME] [--mode mock|integration] [--no-guard] [--fast]
```

| Scenario | OWASP | Story |
|---|---|---|
| `cleanup` | (any) | Claude Code agent deletes `.env` and `.git/` |
| `backup` | ASI-10 | SRE cost-optimizer deletes prod DR backups |
| `wire` | ASI-09 | AP copilot wires $847k to an unverified vendor |
| `freeze` | ASI-10 | Replit-style agent violates declared code freeze, drops prod tables, fabricates replacement rows |

`--mode mock` is the default. `--mode integration` runs the framework-specific example scripts and needs a source checkout.

## sponsio report

Summarize observe-mode session logs into Markdown, HTML, or JSON.

```bash
sponsio report [--since 7d] [--agent NAME] [--format md|html|json] [-o FILE] [--live]
```

Reads `~/.sponsio/sessions/<agent_id>/*.jsonl` and produces a violations summary, top offending contracts, most-violating sessions. Read-only, no network.

```bash
sponsio report --since 24h
sponsio report --format html -o report.html
sponsio report --live --interval 5
```

`--live` cannot combine with `-o`. Malformed JSONL lines and unreadable files are skipped silently.

## sponsio host

Run inside a Claude Code or OpenClaw host plugin.

```bash
sponsio host install <host>           # claude-code | cursor | openclaw
sponsio host install <host> --strict  # refuse tools that have no contract library
sponsio host install <host> --mode observe  # shadow run: log violations, let the tool run
sponsio host status <host>
sponsio host trace <host> [--follow]  # live coloured event stream
```

A tool whose namespace has no contract library (any MCP server outside the
shipped examples) runs with a one-time `running UNCHECKED` warning by
default. `--strict` writes `defaults.unconfigured: deny` into the host
library so those calls are refused instead; the setting survives
reinstalls, and the host library is covered by `capability/self-modify`
so the agent cannot change it. `unconfigured: deny|allow` in the daemon's
`daemon.yaml` overrides it for every library.

The installed hook runs a small shim, `sponsio_shim.py`, under the
interpreter that ran the install (`python -I -S`). The shim forwards each
event to the daemon (see `sponsio daemon` below), starts one when none
answers, and denies the call, with exit code 2 and the host's deny body,
when no daemon can be reached within its deadline (2 s). Every value the
shim needs (socket, plugin root, state dir, deadline) is written on the
hook command, and the shim reads no environment variable, so an `env`
block in the host's settings cannot change it. On Claude Code the
`PreToolUse` entry also carries `"onFailure": "block"` and a 10 s
`timeout`, so a hook that cannot start blocks the call (Claude Code
v2.1.295 or later).

The hook enforces by default. `--mode observe` sets the host's mode in
the daemon's config (`daemon.yaml`, see `sponsio daemon` below). The mode
is not written on the hook command, and the daemon ignores a mode sent
with a call, so editing the hook or the host's `env` does not switch the
guard to observe. Re-run `host install` to switch modes, or to move hooks
installed by an earlier release onto the shim.

While the daemon cannot be reached, every tool call is denied, including
the ones the agent would use to fix it. The deny reason names the
recovery, to run from your own terminal: `sponsio daemon run --detach`,
or `sponsio host uninstall <host>` to remove the hook.

Before `host install` or `host uninstall` changes a host's config file
(Claude Code `settings.json`, Cursor `hooks.json`, OpenClaw
`openclaw.json`), it copies the file to
`<file>.sponsio-backup-YYYYmmddHHMMSS` beside it, then writes the new
version atomically. A config file that is a symlink is written through
to its target. `host uninstall` removes only Sponsio's entries and then
offers to restore the most recent backup, which is the file as it was
before Sponsio last changed it; it asks on a terminal and does nothing
otherwise. A file that holds nothing but Sponsio's entries (one that did
not exist before Sponsio wrote it) is removed outright, with its backups,
since they hold nothing of yours; and a skills directory left empty by
removing the Sponsio skill is removed too.

```bash
sponsio host uninstall <host> --restore-backup     # remove the entries, then put the latest backup back
sponsio host uninstall <host> --no-restore-backup  # remove the entries, don't ask
```

```bash
sponsio host guard <host> [--event E]   # legacy hook entry: same as the shim, through the daemon
sponsio host guard <host> --direct      # debugging: evaluate in-process from the files on disk
```

See [plugins.md](../plugins.md) for the host-plugin walkthrough.

## sponsio plugin

Per-plugin contract library tooling.

```bash
sponsio plugin init                       # bootstraps ~/.sponsio/plugins/_host/sponsio.yaml
sponsio plugin install <name>...          # installs starter packs (github, filesystem, ...)
sponsio plugin install --list             # see what's bundled
sponsio plugin scan <path> --tools t1,t2  # generate library from a plugin's tool set
```

## sponsio doctor

Health checks: install integrity, config syntax, framework wiring.

```bash
sponsio doctor
```

Two checks cover the host hooks. **Hook wiring** reads every Sponsio
hook in the Claude Code and Cursor settings (user and project) and the
OpenClaw plugin config, and checks that each can run: the interpreter
and shim it names still exist, its daemon socket path is short enough to
bind, and a daemon answers or can be started. A hook that cannot run
denies every tool call, so a failure names the fix to run from your
terminal (`sponsio host install <host>` or `sponsio host uninstall
<host>`). **Claude Code** reports the installed version: before v2.1.295
Claude Code ignores the hooks' `onFailure: "block"`, so a hook that
cannot start lets the tool run and only the shim's own deadline applies.

**Enforcement tier** reports which tier the machine is in (see [the threat model](../concepts/threat-model.md)) and what the next tier needs. `sponsio doctor --tier` lists every guarantee of Tier 1, 2 and 3 with pass or fail and the fix (`--json` for a machine-readable form). The checks read the filesystem and the daemon's socket. Tier 1: host hooks go through the daemon. Tier 2 adds: the daemon runs as its own user, this user cannot reach the admin socket, the shim and engine are root-owned and read-only, the rule store belongs to the daemon's user, Claude Code's hooks come from managed settings only, and the host sandbox is on. Tier 3 adds Sponsio's tool gateway and egress proxy, which this release does not include. A default install is Tier 1.

`sponsio host install` refuses to write a hook whose daemon socket path
is too long to bind (more than 103 bytes on macOS, 107 on Linux); set
`SPONSIO_DAEMON_SOCKET` to a shorter path.

## sponsio packs

List shipped contract packs with rule counts and `include:` syntax.

```bash
sponsio packs
```

Reads from `sponsio/contracts/` and prints one row per pack: spec name, tier, rule count, one-line summary. Useful right after `sponsio scan` / `sponsio init` to see what a generated yaml's `include:` lines pull in.

## sponsio eval

Offline trace replay with FPR / FNR scoring. Runs a contract set against recorded traces and reports false-positive and false-negative rates against the upstream ground-truth labels.

```bash
sponsio eval TRACE_PATH [CONTRACTS...] [--config sponsio.yaml] [--agent NAME]
```

Used internally for the [Benchmarks](benchmarks.md) numbers. Also useful for tuning a contract set against your own labelled trace corpus.

## sponsio export

Convert a Sponsio session dump into OTLP for downstream tools.

```bash
sponsio export SOURCE [--to TARGET_DIR]
```

`SOURCE` can be a single session file or a directory. Output is OTLP/JSON ready for ingestion by `sponsio eval` or any OTLP collector.

## sponsio export-sessions

Push session-log files (the JSONL written by `mode="observe"`) to an OTLP endpoint or write them as OTLP/JSON files.

```bash
sponsio export-sessions [--since 24h] [--to PATH | --otlp ENDPOINT]
```

Use `--to PATH` for local files, `--otlp ENDPOINT` for an HTTPS push to your collector. Time windows: `90s`, `30m`, `24h`, `7d`, or `all`.

## sponsio replay

Re-render a recorded session as a coloured terminal view.

```bash
sponsio replay [SESSION] [--config sponsio.yaml]
```

`SESSION` is a session id under `~/.sponsio/sessions/<agent>/`. Without an arg, lists recent sessions. With `--config`, the contracts-armed table shows what each verdict was; without, falls back to the bare event table.

## sponsio explain

Show source, compiled formula, and the last violation for a contract.

```bash
sponsio explain QUERY [--config sponsio.yaml]
```

`QUERY` matches against contract `desc` substrings. Useful when debugging "why is this rule firing?".

## sponsio skill

Install the `sponsio` Agent Skill into the local Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex skill directory. The skill bundles five lifecycle workflows (initial setup, audit and refine, tune in observe, flip to enforce, troubleshoot).

```bash
sponsio skill install [--force] [--link]
```

`--link` symlinks instead of copying, so future `pip install -U --pre sponsio` upgrades the skill in place.

## sponsio mode

Flip a single agent between observe and enforce mode without editing yaml.

```bash
sponsio mode (observe|enforce) [--config sponsio.yaml] [--agent NAME]
```

Equivalent to setting `runtime.mode:` in yaml. The `SPONSIO_MODE` env var still wins over both.

**Parent-aware patching (v0.2)**. The CLI walks the yaml line by line tracking the current top-level key, then:

1. Prefers updating an existing `mode:` line nested under `runtime:`. This is the only line the TypeScript loader reads, so picking the wrong line would silently leave TS stale.
2. Falls back to `mode:` nested under `defaults:` if no `runtime.mode` exists. Both loaders honor this.
3. On a yaml that has neither, appends a fresh `runtime:` block ONLY when target is `observe`. Refuses to append a fresh `enforce` block when no mode line exists and exits 1 with a clear hint. CI scripts that relied on the old exit-1 behavior for malformed configs keep working. To flip a clean yaml to enforce, run `sponsio mode observe` first (which appends the block), then `sponsio mode enforce`.

The walker ignores `mode:` lines nested under unrelated keys (e.g. `judge.fallback_mode:` is not the runtime mode), and preserves inline comments and line endings on the patched line.

## sponsio prompt

Print the agent-facing prompt template for a Sponsio workflow. Used by the `sponsio` skill (W1 initial setup, W2 audit, W3 tune, W4 enforce, W5 troubleshoot).

```bash
sponsio prompt (onboard|scan)
```

Output is a copy-pasteable prompt block your AI assistant can run.

## sponsio serve

Placeholder for the web-dashboard server. This distribution ships the contract runtime + CLI only; the long-lived HTTP backend is not bundled, so the command exits non-zero and points you at the local-inspection alternatives.

```bash
sponsio serve   # prints the alternatives below and exits 2
```

For local observability use `sponsio host trace --follow` (live stream), `sponsio report --since 1h` (session summary), `sponsio replay <session>` (re-render a recorded session), or `sponsio export-sessions` (ship to a collector).

## sponsio daemon

The process that decides host hook calls (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw). It holds the compiled rules, each session's history (in memory, with a write-ahead log, so a restart keeps every live session and deleting trace files does not reset a running one) and its own config. A hook that finds no daemon starts one.

```bash
sponsio daemon run [--socket PATH] [--mode 0600] [--state-dir DIR] [--plugin-root DIR] [--detach] [--watch]
                                                   # foreground; used by launchd/systemd
sponsio daemon ping [--echo VALUE]                 # round-trip health check
sponsio daemon status                              # resolved socket path + reachability
```

Socket path resolves to `$SPONSIO_DAEMON_SOCKET`, then `/var/run/sponsio.sock` if writable, else `~/.sponsio/sponsio.sock`. The state dir defaults to `~/.sponsio/state`. The plugin root is `--plugin-root`, else `~/.sponsio/plugins`; the daemon does not read `$SPONSIO_PLUGIN_ROOT`.

- **Config.** Every setting a hook decision depends on is in `<state-dir>/daemon.yaml`. No environment variable affects a hook decision.
- **Two sockets.** The agent socket above, and an admin socket beside it (`sponsio.sock` becomes `sponsio.admin.sock`, mode 0600) for everything that changes state. The caller's uid, gid and pid come from the kernel, and every admin call is audited.
- **One daemon per state dir.** A second `daemon run` finds the lock taken and exits 0. `--detach` starts it in the background and logs to `<state-dir>/daemon.log`.
- **`--watch`** applies every rule change at once instead of holding weakening ones, for working on Sponsio's own rules. Each change is still recorded.

The `daemon.yaml` schema, both sockets' methods, proposals and every audit event are in the [daemon reference](daemon.md).

## sponsio rules

What the daemon enforces, and rule changes waiting for review. These commands talk to the admin socket, so run them from your own terminal. The agent's hooks deny `sponsio rules reload`.

```bash
sponsio rules status [--json]          # loaded libraries; HELD marks a change waiting for review
sponsio rules diff                     # what a reload would apply: - removed or changed, + added
sponsio rules reload [--bucket B] [--yes]
sponsio rules verify                   # compare with the book the cloud publishes, now
```

The daemon gives every compiled contract a stable id. The id is a hash of the contract's agent, the pack it came from, its formula, strategy and parameters, but not its description. Settings that change decisions (`defaults`, `tools`, `tool_policy`, `runtime`) get ids too. When a library or one of its packs changes on disk:

- If every loaded id is still present, the new rules apply at once, and `ruleset_strengthened` is recorded with what was added.
- If any id was removed or changed, the daemon keeps enforcing the rules it has loaded. It records `config_drift` with the removed and changed contracts and adds a one-line warning to the next hook reply (stderr, and the reason of a deny). The new rules apply only after `sponsio rules reload`, which records `ruleset_reloaded` with the caller's uid and pid. A changed parameter counts as one removal plus one addition. A library that no longer loads counts as removing everything.

Each applied ruleset is kept in `<state-dir>/rules/`. A daemon that starts onto a library weaker than the last applied ruleset, with nothing older in memory, denies that bucket's calls until a reload. `sponsio daemon run --watch` applies every change at once, for working on Sponsio's own rules, and still records each one.

The daemon also polls the library files, their packs and the engine modules on the hook path every 2 s, and records `config_drift` with the old and new SHA-256 of each file that changed. A deleted or truncated trace log is restored from memory and recorded as `trace_deleted`. A call denied by `capability/self-modify` or `capability/host-config-integrity` is recorded as `tamper_attempt`. At Tier 1 these records make tampering visible. They do not prevent it.

With a `cloud:` section in `daemon.yaml`, the daemon also checks every `verify_interval_s` (and on `sponsio rules verify`) that each linked bucket enforces the book the project publishes for its agent. It sends the bucket's contract ids to `POST /v1/rulebook/verify`, and the service computes the published book's ids with the same algorithm. The ids ignore descriptions and whether a contract came from a pack, and keep its mode. The answer is `match`, `stronger` (local additions), `weaker` (published contracts missing locally, recorded as `cloud_drift` and announced on the next hook reply), `incomparable` (different SDK versions disagree) or `unsupported`. This check never runs on the decision path. A failed check is reported as a status and never causes a deny.

## sponsio install --system

Tier 2: Sponsio for the whole machine, out of the agent's reach. Run with `sudo`.

```bash
sudo sponsio install --system [--host claude-code] [--host cursor]
                              [--python PATH] [--package SPEC] [--allow-user-hooks]
                              [--no-migrate] [--dry-run]
sudo sponsio uninstall --system [--keep-state] [--dry-run]
```

`install --system` creates the `_sponsio` user, a root-owned engine in `/opt/sponsio` on a root-owned Python 3.10+ (`--python`), root-owned hook shims, the daemon's private state and its launchd or systemd service. It imports `~/.sponsio/plugins` (unless `--no-migrate`) and writes the host's managed settings. `--package` is what pip installs into the engine: a version spec, a wheel or a source directory. `--dry-run` prints every step and changes nothing. What it sets up and what to know about it: [Running Sponsio on a host](../guides/host-operations.md#tier-2-the-system-install).

## sponsio run --sandbox

Tier 3: start an agent whose only way out is Sponsio.

```bash
sponsio run --sandbox [--workspace DIR] [--writable PATH]... [--keep-env NAME]...
                      [--hide-home] [--socket PATH] -- <agent command>
sponsio run --container -- <agent command>    # inside deploy/tier3's agent container
```

The daemon opens an egress proxy for the run; the agent is not started without one. Inside the sandbox the network is that proxy and nothing else, files are read-only outside the workspace and the `--writable` paths, Sponsio's own state cannot be read, and credentials are removed from the environment (names ending in `_TOKEN`, `_SECRET`, `_PASSWORD`, `_API_KEY`, `_KEY`, and known cloud credentials; the agent's own model key and `--keep-env` names stay). Hook settings (`.claude/settings*.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json` in your home and the workspace) stay read-only even under a writable directory. Linux uses bubblewrap; macOS uses `sandbox-exec` with a profile that denies everything not listed, so the agent cannot ask LaunchServices, AppleEvents or launchd to start a process outside the sandbox. `--container` is for a container that is already the sandbox: it only routes the network through the proxy. Exits with the agent's status.

## sponsio admin

Operator commands. They talk to the daemon's admin socket: at Tier 1 that is your own daemon, at Tier 2 run them with `sudo`. The agent's hooks deny them.

```bash
sponsio admin proposals list [--status pending|approved|rejected] [--json]
sponsio admin proposals show ID
sponsio admin proposals approve ID [--yes]     # applies it; recorded with your uid and the change
sponsio admin proposals reject ID [--yes]
sponsio admin audit verify [--state-dir DIR]   # exit 1 when the chain is broken
sponsio admin cloud-key set [--from-file F]    # the daemon's own cloud key; only a fingerprint is recorded
sponsio admin cloud-key status
```

`audit verify` asks the running daemon, which also checks that the last record it wrote is still in the log. With `--state-dir`, or with no daemon, it checks the file's chain alone. The [daemon reference](daemon.md#audit-events) describes the chain.

## sponsio gateway

The MCP gateway. The daemon runs the agent's MCP servers with the credentials in `<state-dir>/gateway.yaml`, and the host is given one MCP server that lists only the tools the session's state allows.

```bash
sponsio gateway command [--socket PATH] [--state-dir DIR] [--plugin-root DIR]
                                       # print the MCP server entry for the host's config
sponsio gateway tools [--socket PATH]  # the tools a new session is offered, and servers that failed
```

Put the entry `gateway command` prints under `mcpServers` in `.mcp.json` (Claude Code) or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (Cursor), and remove the servers it replaces: their credentials move to `gateway.yaml`. The file format and how listing and calls are decided are in the [daemon reference](daemon.md#mcp-gateway).

## sponsio cursor

Cursor IDE integration. Cursor 1.7+ ships a deny-capable hook system (`hooks.json`); Sponsio plugs in as the command for the relevant pre-* events so every Shell/Read/Write/MCP call is evaluated against the contract library before Cursor executes it.

```bash
sponsio cursor install-hooks            # writes ~/.cursor/hooks.json (or project .cursor/hooks.json)
sponsio cursor guard --event <name>     # runtime hook handler; reads payload on stdin, denies via exit 2
```

---

## TypeScript CLI

The `@sponsio/sdk` package ships a parallel CLI with the same command surface. Same yaml output, same block / allow decisions.

| Python | TypeScript |
|---|---|
| `sponsio init` | `npx @sponsio/sdk init` |
| `sponsio scan` | `npx @sponsio/sdk scan` |
| `sponsio validate` | `npx @sponsio/sdk validate` |
| `sponsio check` | `npx @sponsio/sdk check` |
| `sponsio doctor` | `npx @sponsio/sdk doctor` |
| `sponsio demo` | `npx @sponsio/sdk demo` |
| `sponsio report` | `npx @sponsio/sdk report` |
| `sponsio packs` | `npx @sponsio/sdk packs` |
| `sponsio patterns` | `npx @sponsio/sdk patterns` |
| `sponsio mode` | `npx @sponsio/sdk mode` |
| `sponsio explain` | `npx @sponsio/sdk explain` |
| `sponsio replay` | `npx @sponsio/sdk replay` |
| `sponsio export` | `npx @sponsio/sdk export` |
| `sponsio export-sessions` | `npx @sponsio/sdk export-sessions` |
| `sponsio eval` | `npx @sponsio/sdk eval` |
| `sponsio skill` | `npx @sponsio/sdk skill` |
| `sponsio prompt` | `npx @sponsio/sdk prompt` |

Cross-language scenarios in `tests/cross_language/` validate identical verdicts on both engines. The `@sponsio/sdk` was previously published as `@sponsio/scan-ts`; that package was merged in and the deprecation shim removed.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | Parse error, violation, or missing input |


<!-- ====================================================================== -->
<!-- FILE: docs/reference/daemon.md  -->
<!-- ====================================================================== -->

---
title: Daemon reference
description: daemon.yaml, the agent and admin sockets, proposals, held rule changes, signed rules, the MCP gateway, and the hash-chained audit log.
---

# Daemon reference

Host hooks (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw) are decided by the Sponsio daemon, not in the hook's own process. This page lists what the daemon reads, what it serves on each socket, and what it writes to its audit log. For why it is built this way, see the [threat model](../concepts/threat-model.md) and [the host enforcement path](../concepts/architecture.md#6-host-enforcement-path). For the commands, see [CLI reference](cli.md#sponsio-daemon).

---

## Files

Everything lives under the state dir, `~/.sponsio/state` by default (`sponsio daemon run --state-dir`).

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `daemon.yaml` | Every setting a hook decision depends on. |
| `gateway.yaml` | The upstream MCP servers the gateway runs, with their credentials. See [MCP gateway](#mcp-gateway). |
| `daemon.lock` | An exclusive `flock` while a daemon runs, holding its pid. One daemon per state dir. |
| `daemon.log` | Output of a daemon started with `--detach`. |
| `wal/<session>.jsonl` | Each live session's history, one admitted event per line, numbered by `seq`. Replayed on start. |
| `rules/<bucket>.json` | The last ruleset applied to each bucket: contract ids, content hash, when and how. |
| `proposals/<id>.json` | Rule changes submitted from the agent side, pending or decided. |
| `cloud.key` | The daemon's own cloud API key (`sponsio admin cloud-key set`). |
| `audit.jsonl` | Append-only, hash-chained record of what the daemon did and saw. |

All of these are created owner-only (0600 files, 0700 directories). After `sudo sponsio install --system` the state dir is `/Library/Application Support/Sponsio/state` (macOS) or `/var/lib/sponsio` (Linux), owned by `_sponsio`. The sockets are then `run/agent.sock` (macOS, beside `state`) or `/run/sponsio/agent.sock` (Linux), with the admin socket `agent.admin.sock` beside it.

---

## daemon.yaml

```yaml
mode: enforce            # hosts not listed below
hosts:
  claude-code: {mode: observe}
on_error: deny           # deny | allow: what an evaluation error becomes
unconfigured: null       # deny | allow | null (the host library decides)
plugin_root: null        # overrides --plugin-root when set
trace_ttl_hours: 24
cloud:                   # optional: compare loaded rules with the published book
  project: my-project
  buckets: {_host_claude_code: my-agent}
  verify_interval_s: 300
audit:                   # optional: also send every audit record over OTLP/HTTP
  otlp_endpoint: https://otlp.example.com/v1/traces
  otlp_headers: {x-api-key: "..."}
signing:                 # optional: rule files must be signed by this key
  public_key: "<base64 Ed25519 public key>"
  buckets: ["*"]
egress:                  # optional: hosts the egress proxy may reach
  allow: [api.anthropic.com, "*.github.com"]
```

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `enforce` | Mode for hosts not listed under `hosts`. |
| `hosts.<host>.mode` | | `enforce` or `observe` for one host. Set with `sponsio host install <host> --mode`. `gateway` is the MCP gateway's entry, `sdk` the SDK's `backend="daemon"`. |
| `on_error` | `deny` | `allow` lets a call through when its library cannot be evaluated. Every such call is audited as `fail_open`. |
| `unconfigured` | `null` | `deny` or `allow` for a tool with no library. `null` lets the host library's `defaults.unconfigured` decide. |
| `plugin_root` | `null` | Library root. When unset, the `--plugin-root` the daemon started with, else `~/.sponsio/plugins`. |
| `trace_ttl_hours` | `24` | A session idle this long is dropped with its log. |
| `cloud.project` | | Cloud project the buckets are linked to. |
| `cloud.buckets` | | Host bucket to cloud agent, for `sponsio rules verify`. |
| `cloud.verify_interval_s` | `300` | How often the daemon compares on its own. At least 30. |
| `audit.otlp_endpoint` | | Every audit record is also sent here as an OTLP span, with its chain fields. |
| `audit.otlp_headers` | | Headers for that endpoint, such as an API key. |
| `signing.public_key` | | Base64 Ed25519 public key that signs rule files. See [Signed rules](#signed-rules). |
| `signing.buckets` | `["*"]` | Which buckets must be signed. |
| `egress.allow` | | Hosts the egress proxy may connect to. `github.com` matches itself on ports 80 and 443, `*.github.com` its subdomains, `github.com:22` one other port, `github.com:*` any port. See [Egress proxy](#egress-proxy). |

The daemon re-reads the file when it changes. A missing file, a file that does not parse, and any key that is missing or not valid all take the strict default. The daemon reads no environment variable for a decision, its own included: `SPONSIO_GUARD_MODE`, `SPONSIO_MODE`, `SPONSIO_HOOK_ON_ERROR`, `SPONSIO_UNCONFIGURED`, `SPONSIO_SHIELD_TRACE_TTL_HOURS` and `SPONSIO_PLUGIN_ROOT` do not affect hooks. They still apply to the in-process SDK and to `sponsio host guard --direct`.

`sponsio host install --mode` writes the mode through the admin socket when a daemon answers there (`mode.set`, audited), and writes the file directly when none does.

---

## Sockets

The daemon listens on two Unix sockets. The agent socket is the one hooks use (`--socket`, default `~/.sponsio/sponsio.sock`). The admin socket sits beside it, named `<stem>.admin<suffix>` (`sponsio.sock` becomes `sponsio.admin.sock`), always mode 0600. A method called on the other socket returns `not_found`.

| Socket | Method | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| agent | `ping` | Health check; returns pid and version. |
| agent | `guard.check` | Decide a pre-event and render the host's reply (`stdout`, `exit_code`, and `stderr` when a warning is pending). |
| agent | `guard.observe` | Record a post-event (the tool's output). Never gates. |
| agent | `gateway.list_tools` | The MCP tools a session may call now. See [MCP gateway](#mcp-gateway). |
| agent | `gateway.call_tool` | Decide an MCP tool call, run it upstream when allowed, and record it. |
| agent | `egress.open`, `egress.close` | Open or close the egress proxy for a `sponsio run` session. See [Egress proxy](#egress-proxy). |
| agent | `sdk.check` | Decide a call from `Sponsio(..., backend="daemon")` against the library it names. |
| agent | `sdk.observe` | Record that call's output. Never gates. |
| agent | `sdk.filter_tools` | The tools that SDK session may call now. |
| agent | `proposal.submit` | Validate a rule change as a dry run and store it. Nothing applies. |
| admin | `ping` | As above. |
| admin | `mode.set` | Persist a host's mode in `daemon.yaml` (`claude-code`, `cursor`, `openclaw`, `gateway` or `sdk`). |
| admin | `rules.status` | Loaded libraries, held changes, the last cloud comparison. |
| admin | `rules.reload` | Apply held changes, for one bucket or all. |
| admin | `rules.verify` | Compare linked buckets with the cloud's published books now. |
| admin | `plugin.append` | Merge contracts into a host bucket. |
| admin | `proposal.list`, `proposal.show` | Read proposals. |
| admin | `proposal.approve`, `proposal.reject` | Decide a proposal. Approve applies it. |
| admin | `audit.verify` | Check the audit chain, including that the last record this daemon wrote is still there. |
| admin | `cloud.set_key`, `cloud.key_status` | Store the daemon's own cloud key; show which key it uses, by fingerprint. |

The protocol is a 4-byte big-endian length followed by a JSON body, one request per connection.

### Who is calling

The daemon reads each caller's uid, gid and pid from the kernel when it accepts the connection: `SO_PEERCRED` on Linux, `LOCAL_PEERCRED` and `LOCAL_PEERPID` on macOS. Nothing the client sends is trusted for identity. An admin call runs only for the daemon's own uid or root. Every admin call, allowed or refused, is audited with that identity.

At Tier 1 the daemon runs as the agent's user, so the agent can reach the admin socket. The audit record is what protects you there. At Tier 2 the admin socket belongs to the daemon's own user.

---

## Project layer

For a host hook call, the daemon adds the contracts in the project's `.sponsio/host.yaml` to the bucket's library. The project layer can only add: anything in it that would weaken a protected contract is dropped and recorded as a `tamper_attempt`. See [A protected library with a project layer](config-yaml.md#a-protected-library-with-a-project-layer).

## Proposals

The agent side cannot change rules. `sponsio plugin append` sends `proposal.submit` on the agent socket; the daemon validates the change as a dry run and stores it under `proposals/`. It applies only when `proposal.approve` arrives on the admin socket, which records who approved it and what changed. When the caller can reach the admin socket (Tier 1), `plugin append` approves its own proposal in the same command, and both steps are audited. When it cannot, the proposal waits for `sponsio admin proposals approve <id>`.

---

## Held rule changes

Every compiled contract gets a stable id: a hash of its agent, the pack it came from, its formula, strategy and parameters, but not its description. Settings that change decisions (`defaults`, `tools`, `tool_policy`, `runtime`) get ids too. When a library or one of its packs changes:

- **Every loaded id is still there.** The new rules apply at once. `ruleset_strengthened` is recorded.
- **An id was removed or changed.** The daemon keeps enforcing what it loaded, records `config_drift` with the removed contracts, and adds a one-line warning to the next hook reply. The change applies after `sponsio rules reload`. A changed parameter counts as one removal and one addition. A library that no longer loads counts as removing everything.
- **The daemon restarts onto a library weaker than `rules/<bucket>.json`.** With nothing older in memory to serve, it denies that bucket's calls until a reload, and says so in the deny reason.

`sponsio daemon run --watch` applies every change at once and still records each one. It is for working on Sponsio's own rules.

---

## Signed rules

With `signing:` in `daemon.yaml`, every rule file of a covered bucket needs a detached signature beside it: `sponsio.yaml.sig`, the base64 Ed25519 signature of the file's exact bytes. A file the library includes needs its own. Packs shipped inside Sponsio (`sponsio:...`) need none.

- **A file that is not signed, or signed by another key.** The last rules that passed keep enforcing, and `rules_unsigned` is recorded. With nothing signed loaded, as after a restart, the bucket's calls are denied, whatever `on_error` says.
- **A signed change.** It is handled like any other change: additions apply, removals are held until `sponsio rules reload`.

Verifying needs `cryptography` (`pip install --pre 'sponsio[signing]'`). Without it, covered buckets are denied, not served unchecked. Signing itself happens where the rules are published; the daemon only verifies.

---

## MCP gateway

The gateway puts the daemon between the agent and its MCP servers. The daemon starts the upstream servers itself, with the credentials in `gateway.yaml`, and the agent's host is given one MCP server, the gateway shim. The agent never holds an upstream's credentials, so it cannot call the upstream another way.

```yaml
# <state-dir>/gateway.yaml, mode 0600
servers:
  github:
    command: [npx, -y, "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
    env: {GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: "..."}
    cwd: null          # optional
    timeout_s: 60      # start-up and per-call budget
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `servers.<name>` | One upstream. Letters, digits, and single `-` or `_` between them. `sponsio` is taken. |
| `command` | The argv, as a list or a string split like a shell would. Only stdio servers are supported. |
| `env` | Added to the daemon's own environment for this server. This is where credentials go. |
| `timeout_s` | How long start-up and each call may take. Default 60. |

A server starts on first use and again after it exits. A change to the file applies on the next call, and a server whose entry changed or went away is stopped.

**What the agent sees.** Each upstream tool is listed as `<server>__<tool>`. Claude Code calls it `mcp__sponsio__<server>__<tool>`. Contracts name it `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, as for any MCP tool, and live in the server's own library, `<plugin-root>/<server>/sponsio.yaml`. The `_gateway` library's `defaults` apply to every server, for example `unconfigured: deny`.

**Per session.** One shim process is one session, with its own history under `gateway:<id>`. `tools/list` returns only the tools a call to which the session's current state would admit. A tool behind a `must_precede` is not listed until its prerequisite has run. A call is decided again with its arguments. A call to a tool that is not listed is refused even when its arguments would pass. A refused call never reaches the upstream. When a call changes the list, the shim sends `notifications/tools/list_changed`. In observe mode (`hosts: {gateway: {mode: observe}}`) every tool is listed and every call runs.

**When there is no daemon.** The shim starts one, as the hook shim does. If none answers, `tools/list` returns an error and every call returns an error result.

**Coexisting with hooks.** When Claude Code's hooks are also installed, the hook decides `mcp__sponsio__<server>__<tool>` as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, against the same library.

The gateway alone does not make Tier 3: an agent that can still run commands can reach the network another way. That needs the sandbox runner (`sponsio run --sandbox`) and the egress proxy.

---

## Egress proxy

`sponsio run --sandbox` asks the daemon for a proxy for its session (`egress.open`) and starts the agent where nothing else on the network is reachable. Every connection is one decision before any byte leaves:

- `CONNECT host:port` (HTTPS, and anything else tunnelled) is decided on the destination;
- a plain-HTTP request is decided on the destination, the method and the URL.

The decision is a call to the tool `egress`, with arguments `host`, `port`, `method` and `url`, in the run's own session (history under `egress:<session>`). It passes when the host and port match `egress.allow` and the `_egress` library, if there is one, admits it: contracts such as `arg_blacklist(egress, host, [...])`, `arg_blacklist(egress, url, [...])` or `rate_limit(egress, 100)`. With neither configured, every connection is refused. A refused connection gets `403` with the reason in the body and an `X-Sponsio-Reason` header.

What the proxy holds to:

- **One spelling per address.** A host is a hostname or a dotted-quad IPv4 address, lower-cased. Other spellings of an address (`2130706433`, `0x7f000001`, `127.1`), IPv6 literals and names with userinfo are refused.
- **Resolved once.** The proxy resolves the name itself and connects to that address, so a DNS answer cannot change between the decision and the connection. Loopback, link-local (cloud metadata), unspecified and reserved addresses are refused unless `egress.allow` names the address.
- **Plain HTTP stays plain.** `CONNECT` to port 80 is refused, so a plain-HTTP request always meets the method and URL contracts. The proxy sends the `Host` header of the decided host, forwards exactly the declared body (a chunked upload gets `411`), and then nothing more from the client: one decided request per connection.

TLS is not intercepted. Contracts see where a connection goes, never what it carries; a contract on the contents of HTTPS traffic is out of scope.

A session is what the client names it. Any process that reaches the agent socket can open a new session, with an empty history, for the egress proxy or the gateway. Contracts that count or order calls hold within a session, not across sessions on a machine (corpus vector V15).

Each session gets a Unix socket in the agent socket's directory (mode 0666) and a port on `127.0.0.1`. The Linux sandbox reaches the socket through a forwarder on `127.0.0.1:3128` inside its own network namespace; the macOS sandbox may open only that port.

---

## Audit events

Every line of `audit.jsonl` is a JSON object with `ts` (UTC, ISO 8601), `event` and `pid`, plus the fields below. It also has `seq` (1, 2, ...), `prev_hash` (the previous record's `hash`) and `hash` (the SHA-256 of the record's canonical JSON without `hash`). Editing or removing a record breaks the chain at that point; `sponsio admin audit verify` finds it, and asks the running daemon for the last record it wrote, so records cut from the end are found too. Records from before the chain existed are counted as unchained, not as a break. When the daemon finds that the log no longer holds the last record it wrote (the log was deleted, cut or rewritten), it does not start a new chain: it writes `audit_log_cut` chained to the record it remembers, so `verify` keeps reporting the break however many records follow. A cut made while the daemon was not running is found only by the exported copy (`audit.otlp_endpoint`); at Tier 2 the agent's user cannot write the log at all.

| Event | Written when | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `daemon_start` | A daemon starts and no earlier one is on record. | `socket` |
| `daemon_restart` | A daemon starts after the previous one went away without stopping. | `socket`, `previous_pid` |
| `daemon_stop` | A daemon stops cleanly. | `socket` |
| `admin_call` | Any call on the admin socket other than `ping`. | `method`, `peer` (uid, gid, pid), `ok`, `code`, `params_sha256` |
| `fail_open` | A call was allowed only because `on_error: allow`. | `host`, `tool`, `conversation`, `plugin_id`, `reason` |
| `ruleset_strengthened` | A library change that only added contracts was applied. | `bucket`, `path`, `added`, `content_hash` |
| `config_drift` | A library change removed or changed contracts (`applied` false when held, true under `--watch`). | `bucket`, `path`, `applied`, `removed`, `added`, `summary`, `load_error` |
| `config_drift` | A watched file changed (rule file, pack or engine module). | `file`, `change`, `old_sha256`, `new_sha256` |
| `ruleset_reloaded` | `sponsio rules reload` applied a held change. | `bucket`, `peer`, `removed`, `added`, `content_hash` |
| `trace_deleted` | A session's log was found deleted or truncated and rewritten from memory. | `conversation`, `problem` |
| `tamper_attempt` | A call was denied by `capability/self-modify` or `capability/host-config-integrity`. | `host`, `tool`, `bucket`, `packs`, `reason` |
| `tamper_attempt` (`source: project_layer`) | A project layer tried to weaken a protected contract, or is not the agent's own regular file. Once per file content. | `host`, `source`, `path`, `dropped` |
| `proposal_submitted` | A rule change was proposed. | `id`, `kind`, `peer` |
| `proposal_approved`, `proposal_rejected` | A proposal was decided. `change` is what was applied (the preview, for a rejection). | `id`, `kind`, `peer`, `change`, `params_sha256` |
| `audit_log_cut` | The log no longer held the last record this daemon wrote. | `expected_seq`, `file_seq` |
| `rules_unsigned` | A covered bucket's rule files failed the signature check. | `bucket`, `reason`, `kept_previous` |
| `cloud_key_set` | The daemon was given a cloud key. | `fingerprint`, `peer` |
| `cloud_drift` | A linked bucket lacks contracts the cloud publishes for its agent. | `bucket`, `agent`, `project`, `status`, `published_version`, `missing` |
| `cloud_verified` | A cloud comparison's outcome changed and is not weaker. | same as `cloud_drift` |

Writing is best effort: a full disk does not stop the daemon from deciding. A line left incomplete by a crash or a full disk is ended before the next record, so that record is not lost; `verify` still reports the incomplete line.

---

**Related:** [Threat model](../concepts/threat-model.md) · [Architecture](../concepts/architecture.md#6-host-enforcement-path) · [CLI reference](cli.md) · [Host operations](../guides/host-operations.md)
